messages:
Evan: Heads-up — we should run an initial smoke + cost sweep for a new model landing: `aqua-8b-v2`. Goal: basic correctness, 99th tail < 250ms for seq<=64, and rough $$/k tokens estimate. Can someone pick this up today?

Maya: I can run the smoke. Do you want the default quantization profile (`q4_0`) or try fp16 first? Also limited GPUs on my bench node until 16:00.

Evan: @Maya fp16 preferred for baseline (no quant) then q4_0 as a follow-up. Keep the run small: seq=64 and seq=512 samples. Capture peak mem, p50/p95/p99, and tokens/sec.

Priyanka: Add a tiny tail test as well: a 1-3 token incremental latency sweep to capture KV cache overhead. Also please record throughput with batch sizes [1,4,8].

Maya: Got it. Command I'll use: ```bash
./bench_tool --model aqua-8b-v2 --seq 64 --iters 30 --batch-sizes 1,4,8 --profile=perf.json --quant=fp16
./bench_tool --model aqua-8b-v2 --seq 512 --iters 20 --batch-sizes 1,4 --profile=perf_long.json --quant=fp16
```

Jason: FYI last time we saw a ~12% throughput drop on 8b models when auto-kernel picked `gemm_v2` on newer cudnn. If you see that, try forcing `gemm_v1` in the runtime override: ```json
{"kernel_overrides": {"matmul":"gemm_v1"}}
```

Liam: @Maya also include VM-level perf counters (`nvidia-smi dmon` + `perf stat -e cycles`) for one run so we can correlate. I can help parse if you upload the logs.

perf-bot: perf job queued: https://ci.internal/runs/34912 — will post summary when finished.

Maya: Kickoff started on node bench-03. Running fp16 seq64 first. ETA ~12m. I'll capture mem/throughput + perf counters.

perf-bot: Run complete. Summary: model=aqua-8b-v2 | config=fp16 | seq=64 | batch=1 | p50=42ms | p95=82ms | p99=136ms | tok/s=1450 | peak_mem=9.8GB | tokens_per_dollar_est=1.9M

Maya: fp16 seq64 looks healthy. p99 136ms, tok/s 1450. Moving to seq512 run now.

perf-bot: Run complete. Summary: model=aqua-8b-v2 | config=fp16 | seq=512 | batch=1 | p50=210ms | p95=290ms | p99=420ms | tok/s=320 | peak_mem=11.9GB

Priyanka: seq512 p99 420ms is a bit higher than our target — likely KV spill/attn kernel. Can you attach the perf.json? I'll run a quick profiler diff.

Maya: Uploaded perf.json and perf_long.json to //redwood/srv/bench-results/aqua-8b-v2/2180001234/ — permissions open to eng-runtime.

Jason: Looking at the profiles, we hit a heavier matmul path for long seq. Trying the kernel override brought tok/s from 320 -> 355 on my local repro. Worth trying in the bench.

Maya: Re-ran seq512 with kernel override `gemm_v1`. Results: p50=195ms | p95=260ms | p99=360ms | tok/s=358 | peak_mem=11.8GB. Improvement noted.

Evan: Nice. Can you capture one quantized q4_0 run (seq=64) to get cost comparison? Then publish a short note in the model-catalog with these key numbers + recommended default runtime override.

Maya: Doing q4_0 seq64 now. perf-bot queued job 34913.

perf-bot: Run complete. Summary: model=aqua-8b-v2 | config=q4_0 | seq=64 | batch=1 | p50=48ms | p95=94ms | p99=155ms | tok/s=1200 | peak_mem=6.1GB | tokens_per_dollar_est=2.6M

Priyanka: q4_0 gives better cost but higher latency — expected. Recommend shipping fp16 default with `kernel_overrides: {matmul:gemm_v1}` for low-latency use-cases and q4_0 for cost-sensitive tiers. Document these as runtime profiles.

Evan: Perfect. @Maya can you draft the model-catalog entry with the three profiles (fp16, fp16+override, q4_0) and attach perf artifacts? I'll review and then we can flag for product to enable model variant routing. :thumbsup:

Maya: Will do, uploading a short writeup and the CSVs now. I'll post the link here when done.

perf-bot: Artifacts uploaded: //redwood/srv/bench-results/aqua-8b-v2/2180001234/artifacts.tar.gz

Maya: Published notes: //docs.internal/models/aqua-8b-v2.md — added perf table, suggested runtime overrides, and cost estimates. Ping me for follow-ups.

Evan: Awesome — thanks all. Closing thread after I add a small note about rollout canaries.

Liam: Great job. If product wants canary settings I'll propose batch-size limits and a fallback to q4_0 for degraded capacity.

Evan: Sounds good. Thread closed. :rocket:
